kpis.sub: ALBEMARLE REACHES PRELIMINARY WAGE DEAL IN CHILE (SEP 9)
kpis.label: Albemarle and its Salar union agreed to a new wage offer on the final day of mediation, averting the walkout that had been set to begin Sep 7; members began ratifying the deal Sep 9-10, bringing closure to this year's Chilean labor negotiations. The new, not-yet-seated CEO transition (Ragnar Udd, effective Feb 1, 2027) remains a separate open question

kpis.sub: FREEPORT SLIDES ON COPPER TARIFF UNCERTAINTY (SEP 11)
kpis.label: FCX fell 6.6% to $71.21 after reports the White House still hasn't decided on a Section 232 tariff for refined copper cathodes phased in from 2027, raising doubts the tariff will happen at all. Copper itself eased to ~$6.47/lb — still +41.2% YoY but decelerating from the +47.6% pace reported last week, and down nearly 2% over the trailing month

kpis.sub: MP MATERIALS STOCK EXTENDS SLIDE DESPITE JEFFERIES PITCH (SEP 9-12)
kpis.label: Shares have eased further to the $50-52 range (from ~$54-55 last week and a ~$60 August peak, ~$9.7-9.8B market cap) even as management used the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference (Sep 9) to reiterate MP's position as the only scaled Western NdPr oxide producer with a fully integrated mine-to-magnet platform. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

kpis.sub: XI'S WASHINGTON VISIT NOW WITHIN TWO WEEKS
kpis.label: Xi Jinping is set to arrive in Washington Sep 24 (departing Sep 25) for a compressed visit that skips the UN General Assembly, with rare-earth licensing and the ongoing Chinese supplier shipment halts explicitly on the agenda. Treasury Secretary Bessent says the US expects Beijing to fully meet its rare-earth commitments; the visit lands 47 days before the Nov 10 export-control suspension expiry

themes.title: Xi's Washington visit is now 10 days out
themes.description: Xi Jinping is expected to arrive in Washington late Sep 23 and depart Sep 25 — an unusually compressed visit that skips the UN General Assembly entirely. Rare-earth licensing is explicitly on the agenda; Treasury Secretary Bessent has said the US expects Beijing to fully meet its rare-earth commitments. The visit lands 47 days before China's expanded export-control suspension expires Nov 10, and 99 days before tougher US defense sourcing rules take effect Jan 1, 2027.

themes.title: Chinese shipment halts remain unresolved heading into the summit
themes.description: The Chinese rare-earth suppliers who quietly halted shipments to US buyers in early August — wary of Beijing penalties tied to Responsible Minerals Initiative compliance — have not resumed as of mid-September. Yttrium exports to the US remain roughly half their 2024 level. China separately placed MP Materials and USA Rare Earth on an export-control list back in June, a reminder the friction predates and could outlast this month's diplomacy.

themes.title: A copper tariff the market was pricing in may not arrive
themes.description: Freeport fell 6.6% on Sep 11 on reports the White House still hasn't decided whether to proceed with a Section 232 tariff on refined copper cathodes phased in from 2027 (proposed at 15%, rising to 30% by 2028), after already imposing 50% tariffs on raw copper and derivative products in 2025-26. Losing that tailwind doesn't break the copper thesis, but it removes an upside catalyst the market had partly priced in.

rows.angle: Only US rare-earth mine + processing (Mountain Pass); $500M Apple magnet offtake (shipments from 2027) + $400M DoD convertible preferred (DoD now largest shareholder, ~15%)
rows.watch for: Shares have eased further to the $50-52 range ($9.7-9.8B market cap), down from ~$54-55 last week and the ~$60 August peak, despite management reiterating MP's only-scaled-Western-NdPr-producer position at the Sep 9 Jefferies Global Industrials Conference. The Apple recycled-magnet offtake, DoD 10X plant guarantee (≥$140M EBITDA floor at $110/kg NdPr), the August gadolinium offtake, and the "Project Swarm" drone-magnet initiative (up to 2M drones/year of reserved capacity) all remain intact — the pullback looks like valuation digestion, not a thesis change. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into magnet metals
rows.watch for: Confirmed Sep 1-2 that early-2026 takeover talks didn't proceed given "a high level of uncertainty"; the CEO search under interim chief Pol Le Roux (since Jul 1, following Amanda Lacaze's retirement) has now run more than two months with no permanent replacement named. Shares sit near A$16.26 against a 12-month analyst target of A$17.93 (14 analysts rate it Buy); record FY26 profit on record average rare-earth-oxide selling prices hasn't resolved the leadership overhang

Averted the threatened walkout: Albemarle and its Salar union reached a preliminary wage deal on the final day of mediation (Sep 9), with member ratification voting following immediately — removing the near-term risk to 2026's 70,700t LCE Atacama guidance. New CEO Ragnar Udd still doesn't take over until Feb 1, 2027, and lithium carbonate's Sep 9 dip to $21.73/kg on a surprise Chinese inventory surplus keeps the cycle-timing question open

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: Stock fell 6.6% Sep 11 to $71.21 on reports the White House still hasn't decided whether to proceed with a Section 232 tariff on refined copper cathodes phased in from 2027, on top of the Aug guidance cut (copper to 3.1B lbs from 3.4B lbs) on the delayed Grasberg ramp-up. Copper itself has eased to ~$6.47/lb — still +41.2% YoY but decelerating from the +47.6% pace two weeks ago. The Indonesia life-of-resource extension and the $100B+ market cap remain intact; the tariff decision is now the swing factor to watch, not a resolved tailwind

tiers.label: Developers / Small-Cap — Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: US rare-earth mine-to-magnet aspirant; Texas mine + Oklahoma magnet plant; DoC $1.6B LOI + ~10% equity stake (Jan 2026, priced $17.17)
rows.watch for: Integration underway following the Sep 3 Serra Verde close ($300M cash + 126,849,307 shares). Stock has held near $17.61 ($4.4B market cap) through the following week, still well off its $43.98 52-week high; Thras Moraitis becomes CEO Oct 1. No major new catalyst this week — digesting the dilution and the four-country integration (Brazil, US, UK, France) is now the story

rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa
rows.watch for: Continues pivoting toward rare earths — management still expects the REE value chain to supply most earnings within five years as uranium becomes a minority contributor. Up to $725M in conditional US government support targets White Mesa's separation expansion; pilot output has reached ~29kg of 99.9%-purity Dy oxide, ahead of the 99.5% automotive spec. The Vacuumschmelze (VAC) acquisition still targets an early-2027 close; stock near $14.50

First two of twelve crystallizer superloads arrived at Thacker Pass in early September after shipping from Plymouth, Utah — concrete progress toward the lithium-carbonate crystallization plant. Site now has 1,600+ workers (2,000+ expected by year-end) as construction moves toward peak activity; mechanical completion still targeted late 2027. The Aug Yorkville convertible facility (up to $175M) sits atop the $2.23B DOE loan for near-term liquidity

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate's global benchmark slipped 1.15% to $21.73/kg on Sep 9 amid an unexpected surplus in Chinese inventories — a reminder that 2026's price recovery is not a one-way trade. Copper's YoY gain has also decelerated, easing from roughly +47.6% two weeks ago to about +41.2% now, down nearly 2% over the trailing month. Both metals can still swing sharply on a single mine, policy, or inventory surprise.

bear_case.title: China can flood the market — or freeze the tap
bear_case.description: The same country whose inventory surplus is pressuring lithium carbonate prices is, per ongoing reporting, also the one whose suppliers are still refusing to ship rare earths to some US buyers over fear of Beijing sanctions. Investors betting on either a supply glut or a supply squeeze are making a bet on Beijing's posture, not just on markets — and that posture is exactly what's on the table at the Sep 24 summit.

bear_case.title: Policy tailwinds aren't guaranteed to arrive
bear_case.description: Freeport's 6.6% one-day drop on copper-tariff uncertainty shows how much of the sector's bull case rests on policy that hasn't actually been finalized. The same is true elsewhere: MP Materials' 10X plant EBITDA guarantee, Energy Fuels' $725M conditional government support, and Project Vault's $10B EXIM-backed stockpile are all real, but each carries execution and political risk between announcement and cash landing.

bear_case.title: Leadership and integration overhangs persist
bear_case.description: Albemarle's strike was averted but its new CEO doesn't take over until Feb 2027; Lynas' CEO search under interim chief Pol Le Roux has now run more than two months with no replacement named; and USA Rare Earth is still digesting 126.85M shares of dilution from the Serra Verde close while integrating assets across four countries. None of these is disqualifying on its own, but none is resolved either.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Only fully integrated US rare-earth producer with DoD as top shareholder; shares have now eased two straight weeks to $50-52 from the ~$60 August peak, but the Apple offtake, DoD 10X plant guarantee, and Project Swarm all remain intact after the Sep 9 Jefferies presentation. Reads as valuation digestion, not a thesis break. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: The CEO search under interim chief Pol Le Roux has now stretched past two months with no replacement named, and confirmed takeover talks that didn't proceed removed a possible M&A catalyst. Record FY26 profit on record rare-earth-oxide prices doesn't offset the unresolved leadership vacuum.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: The Chile strike was averted with a preliminary wage deal Sep 9, removing the near-term operating threat that justified Watch last week. Staying in Watch anyway: the new CEO (Ragnar Udd) still doesn't take over until Feb 2027, and lithium carbonate's Sep 9 dip to $21.73/kg on a surprise Chinese inventory surplus is exactly the kind of cycle-timing signal that keeps a good lithium business out of Core for now.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Stock fell 6.6% Sep 11 on doubt the White House will finalize a refined-copper-cathode tariff, layered on the Aug Grasberg guidance cut. Staying Core on the underlying copper macro (+41.2% YoY) and the $100B+ scale, but two consecutive weeks of guidance and policy disappointments make this the name to watch most closely for a further downgrade.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Serra Verde integration is now the whole story — stock has held flat near $17.61 for a full week post-close, a sign the market is in wait-and-see mode on execution across four countries rather than pricing in a fresh catalyst. Weight held; integration risk keeps this speculative.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: No new catalyst this week, but the rare-earth pivot thesis (majority of earnings from REEs within five years, $725M conditional government support, 29kg of 99.9%-purity Dy oxide produced) is unchanged and intact. Weight held; the VAC deal's early-2027 close remains the next real milestone.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: The first crystallizer superloads physically arriving at Thacker Pass is genuine, tangible construction progress, but it's still years from cash flow (mechanical completion late 2027) and lithium carbonate just showed its first sign of oversupply this quarter. Weight held at the sector's smallest speculative size.
